components: RECON operator (reconnaissance: OSINT, network discovery, asset enumeration) -- stable, tool-backed
EXFILTRATOR operator (data extraction, credential harvesting) -- experimental
Arsenal: 35 built-in tools (83 with the optional full set)
architecture_facts: keyless: the AI coding agent already on your machine (Claude Code, Codex, or Hermes) is the backbone, connected in Settings -- no separate API key or second bill required
every headline metric recomputes live from committed JSON via npm run verify-claims, and raw tool transcripts are stripped for privacy so you audit the graded verdict, not raw output
the 8-operator kill chain (recon through analyst) is the architecture the framework is built to grow into, not what ships stable today
recon alone is confirmed stable and tool-backed, with a proven 90.1% pass@1 on the 104-challenge XBEN suite
exploiter, infiltrator, exfiltrator, and ghost run the same tool-backed ReAct engine as recon but are marked experimental, explicitly unproven as a coordinated swarm
egress-scope containment keeps scans from wandering off the authorized target
licensed AGPL-3.0; requires explicit written permission on any system tested
surprising_detail: The 8-operator kill chain (recon, scanner, exploiter, infiltrator, exfiltrator, ghost, coordinator, analyst) is marketed as the framework's shape, but the README is upfront that only recon is proven: it alone hits 90.1% pass@1 on XBEN, while exploiter/infiltrator/exfiltrator/ghost run the identical ReAct engine yet are labeled experimental and 'unproven as a coordinated swarm.' It's the rare security tool that ships its own maturity table instead of claiming the whole chain works.
